key_insight: VQE is vulnerable to adversarial tampering across the cloud workflow, and a unified benchmark shows that noise-manipulating attacks can hurt it far more than parameter- or circuit-level backdoors.
engineering_relevance: For quantum software and cloud deployment teams, this work provides a common red-teaming framework to compare attack severity and prioritize defenses for VQE-as-a-service pipelines.
method: Built VQE-AdvBench, a unified red-teaming benchmark for VQE robustness.
Covers black-, gray-, and white-box attacks across circuit, parameter, and noise/ZNE manipulation.
Evaluated seven attack scenarios on H2 and H3+ using five noise-calibrated IBM backends.
evidence_signal: The benchmark reports a clear severity ranking, with ZNE-related noise attacks amplifying energy error by up to 8.84×, QTrojan by 7.52×, and QDoor by only 1.37×.
watch_item: Results are bounded to specific molecules, ansatz-backend choices, and IBM hardware settings, so attack impact may differ for other VQE configurations or mitigation pipelines.
paper_title: SoK: Adversarial Robustness of the Variational Quantum Eigensolver via Red-Teaming
